brief_context: Provided information on the history of the company.
brief_extract:
Hoover is one of the best known manufacturers of vacuum cleaners
in the world, and the largest manufacturer concentrating solely on
domestic appliances. David Housden, the company’s Public Affairs Manager, told me
something of the fascinating history of the company and how its
name came to be almost synonymous with vacuum cleaning. The first electrically operated vacuum cleaner was made in Eng-
land in the early years of this century, but it was the Hoover
machine, first made in 1908 in the USA, which was destined to
become a household word for upright cleaners all over the world.

brief_context: Co-founder of the company, originally a saddle manufacturer.
Son of W. M. Hoover and co-founder of the company.
Invented an early electrically powered vacuum cleaner.
brief_extract:
Hoover, who were at that time manufacturers of saddles
and harness. The story goes that Murray Spangler, a relative, who
worked for the Hoovers as caretaker in the factory, suffered badly
from asthma, and found that his job of sweeping the floors greatly
aggravated his ailment. Being of an inventive nature, he produced a
crude form of electrically powered vacuum cleaner.

brief_extract:
How-and why-Americans celebrate Thanksgiving Day

Each year, on the fourth Thursday in November, Americans everywhere celebrate Thanksgiving Day. The EAW Director visited Mrs Calvin C Berlin, wife of the Counsellor for Commercial Affairs at the United States Embassy in London, to talk about this great American tradition. Mrs Berlin came herself to greet me at the front door of her elegant residence in a quiet Belgravia square.

brief_context: Visited Mrs Berlin to discuss Thanksgiving traditions.
brief_extract:
How-and why-Americans celebrate Thanksgiving Day

Each year, on the fourth Thursday in November, Americans everywhere celebrate Thanksgiving Day. The EAW Director visited Mrs Calvin C Berlin, wife of the Counsellor for Commercial Affairs at the United States Embassy in London, to talk about this great American tradition. Mrs Berlin came herself to greet me at the front door of her elegant residence in a quiet Belgravia square.

title: Governor
brief_context: Proclaimed the first Thanksgiving festival in 1621.
brief_extract:
The whole family — aunts, uncles, cousins, everybody — got together at Thanksgiving."

Origins of the custom
We discussed the origins of this longstanding American custom. Whilst harvest thanksgiving celebrations were undoubtedly a part of the Pilgrim tradition, it is generally believed that the first Thanksgiving Day was celebrated in America when Governor William Bradford proclaimed a three-day festival in the autumn of 1621 to give thanks for the harvest. On that occasion, the Pilgrims in the tiny Plymouth Colony made their way to their Meeting House where they gave thanks, not just for the harvest but also for their survival through their first year of hard-won religious freedom.

brief_context: Wrote a letter describing the first Thanksgiving harvest celebrations.
brief_extract:
On that occasion, the Pilgrims in the tiny Plymouth Colony made their way to their Meeting House where they gave thanks, not just for the harvest but also for their survival through their first year of hard-won religious freedom. Bountiful harvest
In a letter of 11th December 1621, Edward Winslow wrote: "Our harvest being gotten in, our Governor sent four men on fowling, that so we might after a more special manner rejoice together, after we had gathered the fruit of our labours. They four in one day killed as much fowl as, with a little help beside, served the Company almost a week.

brief_context: Credited with the ultimate establishment of Thanksgiving Day.
brief_extract: George Washington proclaimed 26th November 1789 as the first National Day of Thanksgiving, but still the idea did not catch on. Credit for the ultimate establishment of Thanksgiving Day is generally given to the efforts of Sarah J Hale, editor and founder in 1828 of the 'Ladies Magazine' published in Boston. Her editorials and her letters to President Lincoln resulted in his proclamation in 1863 and those of succeeding Presidents, but it was not until 1941 that the holiday was finally fixed by Congress to take place annually on the fourth Thursday in November.

brief_context: Central figure and planning boss in the novel 'Overload'.
article_title: BOOK ENDS: OVERLOAD by Arthur Hailey
brief_extract: When it comes to people, however, the picture is rather less convincing since some of them could be described not so much as characters but rather as caricatures. Take, for instance, ‘Nim’ Goldman, the story’s central figure. As planning boss of a giant West Coast power utility he has to battle with internal politics as well as with external conservationist opposition in his frantic efforts to head off the threat of a total breakdown in electricity supplies.

brief_context: Mentioned in a hypothetical scenario regarding electricity industry mores.
article_title: BOOK ENDS: OVERLOAD by Arthur Hailey
brief_extract: Goldman may be a ‘good guy’ at heart but the discriminating are likely to find his particular brand of indiscriminate ardour tiresome — if not tedious — and, at worst, tasteless. For an acid assessment of comparative mores, try transplanting in imagination this West Coast Lothario into the ranks of our own dear electricity supply industry (as Queen Victoria might have put it). The resulting scenario would turn the title ‘Overload’ into the understatement of the year.
